pharm: Active immunizing agent / varicella zoster reactivation prevention
quick: 0.5 mL IM into deltoid muscle as a 2-dose series (Month 0 and Month 2 to 6)
2 doses: 0 and 2-6 months (or 0 and 1-2 months for immunocompromised needing rapid protection)
No data; defer vaccination until completion of pregnancy
No data; weigh clinical benefits against risks
>90-97% efficacy against herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia across all age groups >=50 yr

summary: Recombinant herpes zoster vaccine (Shingrix) is a non-live, recombinant subunit vaccine combining varicella zoster virus (VZV) glycoprotein E (gE) antigen with a liposome-based AS01B adjuvant system. It is indicated for the prevention of herpes zoster (shingles) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) in adults aged 50 years and older, and in immunocompromised adults aged 19 years and older. Because it is a non-live vaccine, it is safe to administer to immunocompromised individuals (unlike the obsolete live Zostavax). Given intramuscularly in 2 doses separated by 2 to 6 months.
indications: Prevention of herpes zoster (shingles) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) in adults aged 50 years and older
Prevention of herpes zoster in adults aged 19 years and older who are or will be at increased risk of herpes zoster due to immunodeficiency or immunosuppression caused by known disease or therapy
Recommended regardless of prior history of herpes zoster or prior vaccination with live zoster vaccine

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at Month 0 and Month 2 to 6
dosage.n: Minimum interval between doses is 4 weeks. If more than 6 months have elapsed since dose 1, administer dose 2 as soon as possible without restarting the series.

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at Month 0 and Month 1 to 2
dosage.n: Shorter 1- to 2-month interval may be utilized in patients who would benefit from completing the series prior to initiating anticipated immunosuppression.

admin: Must be reconstituted prior to administration: withdraw entire contents of the adjuvant suspension vial and transfer into the lyophilized gE antigen vial. Swirl gently until fully dissolved.
Administer strictly intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle. Do NOT administer intravenously, intradermally, or subcutaneously.
Administer immediately after reconstitution or store refrigerated (2°C to 8°C) and use within 6 hours. Discard if not used within 6 hours.
Warn patients that local reactogenicity (soreness, swelling) and systemic fatigue/fever are common but transient (1-3 days).
moa: By combining recombinant VZV glycoprotein E (the most abundant envelope glycoprotein on VZV virions and infected cells) with the novel AS01B adjuvant system (containing QS-21 saponin and 3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A in liposomes), the vaccine stimulates high-titer gE-specific neutralizing antibodies and long-lived, antigen-specific CD4+ T-cell-mediated cellular immunity that prevents latent VZV reactivation in sensory dorsal root and cranial nerve ganglia.

absolute: Severe acute anaphylactic hypersensitivity to any component of the vaccine or after a previous dose of Shingrix
relative: Current active herpes zoster episode (defer vaccination until acute illness and symptoms have completely resolved)
Moderate to severe acute febrile illness (defer until recovered)
Pregnancy (defer until postpartum due to lack of safety data)
monitor: Pronounced local injection site pain, erythema, swelling (very common, >75%)
Systemic myalgia, fatigue, headache, shivering, low-grade fever, gastrointestinal symptoms

preg: No human safety data. Vaccination should generally be deferred until after pregnancy.
lact: Unknown whether vaccine components or antibodies are excreted in human milk. Consider clinical benefits and maternal risks.
renal: No dose adjustment required. Safe in end-stage renal disease and hemodialysis.
serious_se: Severe systemic reactogenicity preventing normal daily activities (typically resolves within 2-3 days)
Small statistical association with Guillain-Barré syndrome (estimated ~3 excess cases per million doses in adults >=65 yr)
monitoring: Observe patient for 15 minutes post-injection for acute hypersensitivity
Reassure patients about reactogenicity to prevent non-compliance with the second mandatory dose
